description: THE MOST EVIDENTIALLY VALUABLE PHOTOGRAPH IN THE SURVEY TO DATE — A PAINTED ROSTER ROCK. A massive boulder at a fortified summit position, its face covered in hand-painted panels of names and insignia, topped by a sandbagged bunker; barbed wire strung below, a steel ladder at right leading up behind the rock, guy wires crossing the sky. The panels include an American roster, Vietnamese rosters with unit numbers, a site-opening date, painted parachute wings, and a painted unit shield. This one photograph may identify the site, its opening date, and much of its garrison by name.
